result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Calculate current-flow betweenness counting only flow from given sources to targets. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Calculate current-flow betweenness counting only flow from given sources to targets. title: >- [Graph.current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Calculate current-flow betweenness counting only flow from given sources to targets. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate current-flow betweenness counting only flow from given sources to targets. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L47365-L47466){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset( sources, targets, normalized=True, weighted=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Current-flow betweenness on a subset](../assets/graphs/current-flow-betweenness-centrality-subset.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph with the sources A and B and the target G outlined; only current sent from A or B to G counts. All of it passes E and F, which share the top at 0.067, while inside the triangles it spreads over every route: C 0.043, D 0.030, and even the sources pass some of each other's current, B 0.014 and A 0.006." width="100%"} `current_flow_betweenness_centrality()` sends a unit of electrical current between every pair of nodes and credits each node with the current passing through it. This variant only sends current from each node in `sources=` to each node in `targets=`, so it asks which nodes carry the flow between two particular sets: say, the junctions a rumor passes through on its way from one community to another, or the substations between a set of power plants and a set of cities. Like the full measure, it credits every route in proportion to its conductance, not only the shortest ones. A node's share of a source-target flow is half the current on its edges; the source and target themselves get nothing for their own pair. Edge weights act as conductances. The graph must be undirected and connected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [sources]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Nodes that inject current, as integer IDs or string labels. [targets]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Nodes that extract current, as integer IDs or string labels. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), divide by `(n - 1)(n - 2)`, as for the full measure. If `False`, return half the total over all source-target pairs. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights as conductances. If `None` (default), follows the graph. Weights must be positive. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store scores in. If `None` (default), uses `"current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the scores as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or disconnected, a node does not exist, or a weight is not positive. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The potentials for a unit current from `s` to `t` come from the pseudo-inverse of the Laplacian (grounded at one node), so each pair costs $O(E)$ after an $O(V^3)$ factorization. With every node as both a source and a target the scores equal `current_flow_betweenness_centrality()`, normalized or not. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a square with one diagonal, current from `A` to `C` mostly takes the diagonal, but some still flows around through `B` and `D`: ::: {#ab4201ba .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec square = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "A"), ("A", "C")]) ) scores = square.current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset(["A"], ["C"], return_dict=True) {square.get_label_from_id(n): round(s, 3) for n, s in sorted(scores.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 0.0, 'B': 0.042, 'C': 0.0, 'D': 0.042} ``` ::: ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} NetworkX's `current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset()` also counts the current at each pair's own source and target and then subtracts the constant `1 / (n - 2)` from every node, which removes the endpoint share only when every node is both a source and a target. Its results agree with EdgeCase's in that case and otherwise do not.
